## TL;DR

QA-checked the Agents page's three in-scope surfaces (agent list, Model
providers, Model routing) at 375, 768 and 1280px with headless WebKit against
fixtures only, and shipped the harness as a permanent 12-case regression test.
Five real defects found and fixed: the on/off switch lost its pill shape on
phones (a #1139 touch-target side effect), the Model providers tab showed a
spurious "No usage reported yet." under real usage data, the Model routing tab
let a section heading run into its first checkbox, placed one field's label
inconsistently beside its input, and truncated the pasted-key placeholder at
375px. `repoos check --changed main` is green. `docs/qa/2026-11-agents-routing-qa.md`
records scope, method, findings and the not-verified list.

## Work and rationale

The task demanded "headless Playwright only against fixtures", and the repo
already had the right pattern: `task-create-edit-browser.test.ts` mounts the
real component in jsdom with fixture data, extracts the rendered markup plus
compiled scoped styles, and renders that markup in headless WebKit with the
real built global stylesheet. I reused it for a new
`src/ui-app/tests/agents-page-qa-browser.test.ts` with four fixtures:

1. the default agent list with a failed run and a previous-setup run (both
   run details expanded, since the expanded text is exactly what must stay
   readable),
2. Model providers covering missing-key (OpenRouter, Jev), healthy keyed
   usage (opencode Go), a CLI-login row with an unavailable session (Muse),
   a failed usage fetch (DeepInfra) and a link-only row,
3. Model routing in the missing-key state with the key form opened,
4. Model routing in the provider-failure state: a failed live probe plus
   four recent decisions (applied, provider-failure fallback, blocked,
   shadow) with one expanded.

Each fixture is audited at all three widths: no document horizontal overflow,
no element past the viewport (excluding horizontal scrollers and closed
`<details>` content, which WebKit lays out but never paints — it
false-positived until I covered the open state explicitly), plus per-state
content assertions. Every credential surface is asserted masked:
`type="password"`, realistic placeholders, and Saved / Not set pills only.
Fixtures only — no real key was read or printed anywhere. I set `QA_SHOTS`
to capture full-page screenshots per fixture and width and inspected all of
them by hand before turning findings into assertions.

## Approaches tried

For the switch fix I first tried overriding the thumb with
`transform: translateX(22px)` and then with the `translate: 22px` shorthand;
both failed for interesting reasons. Tailwind v4 emits `translate:
var(--tw-translate-x)` (a *separate* property from `transform`), so a
`transform` override adds to Tailwind's value instead of replacing it — the
thumb travelled 40px and overflowed the root. The `translate` shorthand was
then dropped entirely by the CSS minifier, which downlevels it. The fix that
survived both: retarget the `--tw-translate-x` custom property the utility
reads, with the thumb absolutely positioned inside the drawn track. This is
recorded in a code comment because it will bite the next person who tries.

## Challenges and blockers

- The scoped-CSS harness needs the built UI stylesheet, so the test depends
  on `dist/ui` existing — the established repo pattern, and `repoos check`
  builds before tests.
- Playwright's `expect(locator).toContainText(...)` matchers are not
  registered in this repo's vitest setup, so text assertions are manual
  (`textContent()` + vitest matchers). One locator that auto-waits for a
  missing element consumed a 30s test timeout before I noticed; the DeepInfra
  failure fixture needed `{ ok: false }` because `api()` throws on non-ok.
- The first full `repoos check` failed on `rendered-contrast`; in isolation
  the step passed, and the full re-run passed, so I treated the single
  failure as contention (per `docs/debugging-check-failures.md`) rather than
  patching blindly. No source change was involved between the runs.
- The routing fixture initially paired a saved credential with a
  missing-key issue notice, which the real server never emits — I checked
  `modelRoutingStatus()` and made the fixture match real server behaviour.
- The first handoff attempt failed twice on infrastructure, not on the
  fixes: the report draft had a title line before `## TL;DR` (blocked at the
  review step), and the declared providers shot reported `missing-target`.
  The highlight check is an instant in-page evaluate, so under machine load
  it ran before the panel's `/api/model-providers` fetch resolved and the
  opencode-go row did not exist yet. I re-declared all three shots with an
  explicit `waitFor` step on the highlight's own selector (a real Playwright
  locator wait with a 5s timeout, strictly stronger than the instant check).
- The branch sat 177 commits behind main when I resumed; I merged main in
  (clean, no conflicts), rebuilt, and re-ran the 12-case browser test and
  both panel suites against the merged tree before re-checking.

## Key learnings

- A 44px touch-target rule applied to a Radix switch destroys its aspect
  ratio; the fix is to keep the hit area and draw the visual track inside it,
  not to shrink the target back below 44px.
- Tailwind v4's translate utilities live in the `translate` CSS property, and
  this repo's minifier downlevels that shorthand — override the custom
  property, not the property.
- Closed `<details>` content is laid out but unpainted in WebKit, so geometry
  audits must exclude it and instead cover the *open* state, which is the
  state a user actually reads.
- Fixture fidelity matters: an inconsistent fixture (saved key + missing-key
  issue) makes the UI look buggy when the server would never produce that
  combination. Verify fixtures against the server code that produces the
  shape.

Left for review: the full diff is the new browser test, five small CSS/markup
fixes, and the QA document. No `repoos.toml` change, no new dependency.
